transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AuroraScale - Head Partnerships), Jason Wu (AuroraScale - Solutions Architect), Amir Khan (AuroraScale - BD)
Recording id: ff-20260721-aurorascale-01

Summary (auto):
Quick partner intro between Redwood and AuroraScale. Discussed potential partnership patterns (cloud reseller, co-marketed dedicated offering), AuroraScale's customer base (SIs and regulated enterprise), technical constraints (VPC/on-prem, HSM/KMS, data residency), initial integration ideas, and next steps to schedule an SE deep-dive and share artifacts.

Topics: partner motion, technical integration (VPC, peering), dedicated vs hosted routing, security/compliance, pricing/throughput expectations.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining. um this is Lena from Redwood, AE, and I've got Mateo here our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya (AuroraScale): good thanks, Lena. excited to learn more, we've heard a lot about the redwood runtime from partners.
[00:10] Jason (AuroraScale): yeah thanks. we wanted to understand partner options and what integrations look like for our cloud + gpu resale channel.
[00:16] Mateo (Redwood SE): awesome. quick agenda — intro, partner program outline, a little on the serving runtime and controls, then technical constraints and questions. we'll finish with next steps. sound good?
[00:24] Amir (AuroraScale): yep, perfect.
[00:26] Lena: cool — quick context on AuroraScale for us, priya? you can tell us typical customers and what you see in the field.
[00:31] Priya: sure — we primarily sell to SIs and mid-enterprise who need GPU-backed inference. there's a lot of regulated workloads — healthcare, finserv, gov — so data residency and audit trails matter. we also do managed private deployments for some larger accounts.
[00:46] Jason: and technical note: many customers want an opinionated stack that simplifies triage. they prefer either a hosted model they can resell, or a co-managed dedicated pool that sits in their VPC.
[00:57] Mateo: that's helpful. Redwood's partner motions typically cover three patterns — hosted API reseller, Dedicated reserved pools for partners, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customers. our runtime supports routing and fallbacks between variants so you can offer safer SLAs.
[01:12] Priya: how much control do partners get over pricing and SLAs on the hosted product?
[01:16] Lena: good question. for hosted reseller we provide an API + partner pricing tier; partners can white-label or bundle with managed services. SLA options are more between Redwood and the buyer in dedicated/private motions. we can share the partner program doc — there's a one-pager I'll send after this. link noted.
[01:29] Jason: nice. technical question — for dedicated pools, do you support bringing your own infra (BYOI) into our VPC, or is it only Redwood-managed?
[01:36] Mateo: we have both. Redwood Dedicated can be provisioned in a couple ways — hosted in our cloud with isolated pools, or Private deployment where the control plane lives in your account (we term it Redwood Private). For BYOI there's an on-prem option with a private control plane and kms integration. sometimes the wording is confusing in docs — we call it Redwood Private and Redwood Dedicated, naming differs in notes.
[01:52] Priya: perfect. and latency/cost tradeoffs — customers often ask whether to serve from hosted vs dedicated. what guidance do you give?
[01:58] Mateo: generally dedicated reduces multi-tenant variance and gives predictable throughput, which helps latency SLOs. hosted is easiest for time-to-market and often cheaper at lower scale. we also have batching, KV cache (some transcripts say K V cash ha) and prefix caching to reduce tokens. our Optimize toolkit gives recommendations — quant profiles, batching policies by workload.
[02:19] Amir: do you do quantization strategies in-house or rely on partners?
[02:22] Mateo: we have recommended quant profiles and tests for common models; we can work with partners on model quantization and kernel selection. we also do continuous batching at runtime so sometimes quant + batching yields best unit economics.
[02:32] Jason: on compliance — SOC2, ISO, audit logs, SSO — do you provide audit logs and KMS integration we can show customers?
[02:38] Lena: yes — we support audit logs, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. Redwood Private mode gives you the ability to keep control of keys, and we produce audit trails per-request. I'll attach our security deck.
[02:49] Priya: awesome. client asks frequently about data retention and model training — do you allow fine-tuning or expose logs for model retraining of customer data?
[02:58] Mateo: Redwood's hosted API by default doesn't train on customer data; retention is configurable and we have options for customers to opt-in for training. For partners we recommend Private deployments when customers need strict no-training guarantees. also we support redaction and token-level cost breakdowns in Console.
[03:15] Jason: practical integration question — networking. can you peer into our VPC? what's the common pattern?
[03:20] Mateo: common patterns: VPC peering, PrivateLink, or site-to-site VPN for on-prem. For Private we provision a control plane that runs in your account, so peering is minimal. We'll need a diagram of subnets and egress rules to validate.
[03:33] Priya: we'll share a network diagram — Jason will upload it after this call.
[03:36] Jason: yes, will do.
[03:38] Amir: curious — any big customers you can name that do co-managed dedicated pools?
[03:42] Lena: we have a few telco and fintech customers on dedicated pools, and several healthcare customers on Private. I can share anonymized case studies in the partner pack.
[03:51] Priya: great. can you walk through a quick example of throughput/latency expectations for, say, a 13B model at 8k context vs 32k?
[03:57] Mateo: rough numbers — depends on hardware and quant. On an A100 class or equivalent, polyester — sorry, got my notes — on A100-like hardware a 13B unquantized might do dozens to low hundreds of tokens per second depending on batch. With int8 or int4 we can see 2-4x token throughput improvements. For >16k contexts we need to consider KV cache memory footprint; sometimes kernel selection and sequence parallelism change. I'd like to do a small benchmark with your expected prompt mix.
[04:25] Jason: yeah a bench would be useful. we have customers asking for concurrency of ~50-100 qps for short chat use cases, and others with long context summarization.
[04:33] Mateo: for 50-100 qps you usually design dedicated pools with autoscaling and an autoscale burst; we can provide sizing guidance. also we have smart routing so you can route some traffic to cheaper model variants for non-critical requests.
[04:44] Priya: what about shared models / licensing? do you have a catalog partners can resell?
[04:48] Lena: we have a curated catalog with verified performance profiles. partners can choose which models to surface; we also support bringing customer models for Private deployments. Pricing is usage-based for hosted, reserved for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private. I'll include pricing examples in the follow-up.
[05:01] Amir: do you support marketplace integrations or billing connectors?
[05:04] Lena: yes — we have cloud marketplace listings and can integrate with partner billing flows in many cases. it's often a negotiation for enterprise partners.
[05:10] Jason: any pre-reqs from our side for a POC? what data should we gather?
[05:14] Mateo: a typical POC needs: sample traffic/profile (prompt lengths, qps, % streaming), dataset for quality checks, acceptance criteria (latency, cost per 1K tokens, failure rate), and network diagram. we'll also want to agree on model variants to test.
[05:27] Priya: sounds good. for our channel customers, security and managed key control are big. we'll prioritize Private for few accounts and Dedicated/reseller for others.
[05:36] Lena: great — for partners we often start with sales enablement + a joint pilot. I'll send a partner one-pager and the security/compliance deck. Mateo will drive the bench.
[05:45] Jason: perfect.
[05:47] Amir: quick question — competitors. we sometimes get asked to compare to Lambda or Paperspace — what's the typical differentiation?
[05:52] Mateo: the main differentiators are production-first serving runtimes, unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private, and tooling around cost/perf (Optimize). competitors might give self-hosted runtimes or simpler endpoints but less unified orchestration. also our fallback policies and rollouts are tuned for reliability.
[06:08] Priya: understood. any red flags we should be aware of from a partner enablement perspective?
[06:12] Lena: just the normal onboarding: ensure SLA expectations are aligned, define support matrix, and agree on co-marketing assets. we'll provide enablement materials and a partner playbook.
[06:22] Jason: can you send a sample contract or partner terms?
[06:25] Lena: yes we'll send the partner terms and a sample MOU after this call.
[06:28] Priya: great. okay let's capture next steps.
[06:31] Speaker 1: (automated) action items captured.
[06:33] Lena: recap — Lena to send partner one-pager + security deck + sample terms (by Fri 7/23), Mateo to run bench estimates and prepare a short tech-deep dive deck (by 7/28), AuroraScale to send infra diagram and list of 2-3 pilot customers (by 7/24). we'll aim to schedule the SE deep-dive for week of 7/27.
[06:55] Jason: that works. thanks everyone.
[06:58] Priya: thanks all.
[07:00] Amir: thanks.
